newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela develops new heavy crude technology.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela develops new heavy crude technology.

text.p: Venezuela's Petroleos de Venezuela has begun a new round of tests on technology which will reduce costs and improve efficiency in the upgrading of its massive heavy and extra heavy crude reserves, PDVSA sources said.
"It is a process of treating heavy crudes at high temperatures and low pressure to obtain a product with high commercial value," one source said.

Tests on the patented Aquaconversion TM technology, which PDVSA has been developing through its investigation and technology unit Inevep for the last 10 years, are being carried out at PDVSA's Isla refinery in Curacao this week, the source said.
The new technology should reduce production and transport costs during the process of upgrading the crude.
It will allow crude to be upgraded either at the point of extraction or before being exported, another PDVSA source said.
"It's an extremely competitive technology," he said.
At least 70 percent of PDVSA's proven oil reserves of 73 billion barrels are heavy and extra heavy crudes and bitumens.
In addition PDVSA estimates that it has about 270 billion barrels of recoverable oil in the Orinoco Tar Belt.
PDVSA has signed five deals with major oil corporations for upgrade projects in the Orinoco Tar Belt and is thought to be considering at least three more.
